sources.entry: ImgCompress - Image processing tool that runs entirely in Docker. Compress, convert, resize, batch-process images, and remove backgrounds using local AI without cloud dependencies. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: ImgCompress is a self-hosted image processing server, packaged as a single Docker container, that converts 70+ image formats, compresses and resizes in bulk, crops per file, and removes backgrounds with a bundled local AI model.
summary.what_it_does: The tool runs as a single Docker container and provides a browser dashboard plus a CLI for scripting. It converts between 70+ formats, including HEIC, HEIF, PSD, AVIF, EPS, PDF, WebP, TIFF, BMP and GIF, and can turn image batches into a paginated PDF. Bulk compression uses multi-core parallel processing. Each uploaded file can be cropped individually with ratio presets (Free, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3) or custom pixel dimensions before conversion. Background removal runs on the CPU with a bundled model and needs no API key or upload. The README says the UI is available in 12 languages and that the container works offline once pulled.
use_cases: convert HEIC photos to WebP or JPG
crop batches of images to set aspect ratios
how_to_run: Optional: use docker/compose/proxied.docker-compose.yaml for HTTPS behind Traefik
notable: Runs entirely in one container with no host dependencies and no telemetry
Per-file crop editor with saved crops that can differ within one batch
Bundled local AI background removal with no cloud calls
Hardened image: no shell, no curl/wget, non-root user, SBOM and provenance attestation
caveats: Some formats such as PSD and EPS are rendered server-side before cropping
Background removal runs on CPU, and the README does not give performance figures
The README mentions a paid cloud server via xCloud, but the software itself is free
